sentences.text: Rhaeticosaurus, meaning 'Rhaetian lizard', is an extinct basal pliosauroid found in Late Triassic rocks of the Exter Formation.
Based on the holotype — the specimen the species is based on — this animal reached a maximum length of 2.37 meters when fully grown.
The animal is known from a partial articulated skeleton, preserving the bones in their original positions.
Its discovery site was located about 3.5 meters below a bonebed containing Rhaetian-age vertebrate fauna.
The genus Rhaeticosaurus was named by Wintrich and colleagues in 2017, with the type species being Rhaeticosaurus mertensi.
The holotype specimen is cataloged as LWL-MFN P 64047 and was discovered in 2013 in Clay pit #3, which belonged to the Lücking brick company.
Rhaeticosaurus lived during the Rhaetian stage, between 205.7 and 201.4 million years ago.
